info.title: WeaveSignal control plane API
info.description: The station's HTTP API, `/api/v1` (ADR-0195). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only. Bodies are JSON. The narrative (authorisation, errors, stability) is in the product documentation's *Control plane routes* page.

get.description: Open: what the public pages show anyway. The accent colour and the addresses of the brand icon and the banner, each `null` until set. A station without a database answers with all three `null`.

put.description: Admin only. One sRGB colour as six hex digits. The pages derive each theme's accent from it (its lightness moved until it reads at 4.5:1), so any colour is accepted. Empty goes back to the product's own.

get.description: Open. The PNG the station made from the upload. Under the version its address carries (`?v=`, from `GET /api/v1/branding`) it may be kept for good; `404` when the station has set none.

put.description: Admin only. The body is the picture itself, a PNG or a JPEG (recognised by its first bytes; nothing else is read, and never SVG). At most 4 MB, at least 600 by 200 pixels; it is cropped about its middle to three to one and fitted inside 1,200 by 400. The station stores and serves the PNG its media worker writes, never the upload, so no metadata survives.

get.description: The station's banks and carts, which every show shares, and with `show` that show's own beside them (each owner's banks are numbered 1 to 5 apart; a bank or cart names its show, or `null` for the station's). A studio window asks for its show: a live window the show the station's step comes from, a preparing window the show it prepares. Each cart with FILE MISSING. Fetch it again when the studio view's `carts.version` moves.

put.description: A bank of the station's, shared by every show. A show's own banks are `/api/v1/shows/{show}/carts/banks/{number}`. Answers with the station's catalogue.

post.summary: Fire, stop or cue a cart
post.description: `toggle`, `fire`, `stop`, `cue` a cart; `stop_last`; `fade_all`; `clear_cue`. Carts sound in the desk (ADR-0117). A cart in a show's own bank starts only while that show is the one the station's step comes from (409 otherwise); anything sounding can be stopped. Answers with the new studio view.

500.description: The cart wall failed.

post.description: A chat mode (`slow`, `hold_new`, `links_trusted`) on or off, or influx (five settings at once, the earlier ones back when turned off, ADR-0068). The studio's modes; the chat service reads them. Answers with the new studio view.

The same requests as the desk's control socket, without `status`: `on_air`, `mute`, `cue`, `talk`, `talk_to`, or `dump` the profanity delay. Answers with the new studio view. A caller cannot go on air or in cue without their consent to record on file (409). The show on air's step switches some off (409, ADR-0271): `dump` below `callers`, the handover (the next DJ going on air) and `picture` below `full`, where the picture is held on the slate.

get.summary: The programme sent to another Icecast server
get.description: ADR-0226: whether the station sends its programme, as an Icecast source, to a server of the deployment's choosing (a DJ's AzuraCast). Says whether it is set up, the station's choice (`auto`, `on`, `off`), whether it is sending now and why, whether the remote server took the login, the last error in words, and bytes sent. The server's password is never in the answer. Any signed-in staff may read it.

put.summary: Choose when the programme is sent to another Icecast server
put.description: Admin only. The choice is kept across restarts. It takes effect at once. The server's address, user and password are the deployment's settings (`ICECAST_OUT_*`), not this route's.

200.description: The outgoing source after the change.

500.description: The database refused.

post.description: A link for a guest, a remote DJ or a presenter. A caller joins another way (422). The show on air's step decides which seats can be invited (ADR-0271): below `guests` a guest or a second presenter is refused, below `full` a DJ is, each with 422 and `field` `role`; the pass is checked again when it is used. With `for_me` the invitation is a presenter's for the signed-in account, allowed at every step for the show's presenter (403 for another account at Solo, 422 for the station key); it is the Solo DJ's own microphone link.

500.description: The database refused.

put.description: An audio file as the body, the track's words in the query: the media worker normalises it into the library.

get.description: Server-sent events: a `now_playing` event whose data is the same JSON as `GET /api/v1/now-playing`, at once and on every change.
This document: the API as OpenAPI 3.1, generated from the handlers. Needs no bearer; the description is not secret.

The pass is the bearer: from an invitation's link or a call-in. Says who it is for and whether the studio has ended it. `not_now` says why the pass cannot join yet when the show on air runs at a step that has switched its seat off (ADR-0271); the pass stays good for later.

Someone already in the room is never refused.

post.summary: Hand the air to automation, or take it back
post.description: Sets the station's mode (ADR-0045) without changing any other playout setting, and answers with the new studio view. Any staff member's: `PUT /api/v1/playout/settings` stays an admin's. Anyone on air at the desk is not taken off air; in `auto` the desk is simply not heard, and in `live` it is heard again at once. The change is immediate (profanity delay and all); End show (`POST /api/v1/show/end`) is the route that takes people off air and waits for the delay. 503 when the station has no playout layer.

post.summary: A room token for one person
post.description: A short-lived LiveKit token for one person, with their role in it for the desk to read. A `listener` token is a monitor that hears every return (ADR-0118): only an admin may ask for one (403 otherwise). A `caller` token records the caller's consent on the station's behalf, against the words the station shows now (`consent`). A `guest`, `dj`, `screener` or `caller` token for a seat the show on air's step has switched off is refused (409, ADR-0271), unless that person is in the room already.

get.description: Admin only. Every destination (never its stream key) with the desk's view of it (`desk`: its state, the last error with the key cut out, the bytes sent), whether the desk runs video (RTMP out needs it), the encoders running, and each platform's form.

post.description: Admin only. `name`, `platform`, `url` (the server URL, `rtmp://` or `rtmps://`), `key` (the stream key, sealed in the database and never shown again), `profile` (`compatible`, the default, or `open`) and `enabled` (off unless asked). At most 10 (409); a name in use is 409 too.

Sets whether this session's window is preparing a show (ADR-0276). A preparing window can look at the live desk but not drive it: the desk's commands, the carts' commands, the screener's commands, ending a pass or the show, and the station's mode are refused (409) until it is live again. Everything about the person's own show stays open. A session starts live. Answers as `GET /api/v1/sessions/me` does. The station key is always live, and so is an API token: 422.

put.description: Admin only. The chat reads the name when it next starts. A field left empty goes back to the settings file's value.

put.description: Admin only. Only where the install route has a stream password (the Cloudron package; elsewhere `409`). The answer is written to a file the package's start script reads, so it applies when the station next restarts. The password is never read back. A password-protected stream is silent in the player page: a browser does not ask for a password for audio from another name.

post.description: Takes everyone off air (presenters, DJs, guests, callers; callers stay in the room and the queue), fades every cart, then hands the air to automation by setting the station's mode to `auto`. The switch waits for the profanity delay to play out, so the last words are heard; `automation_in_ms` says how long. If somebody has gone back on air by then the switch is skipped, and the studio gets a notice saying why. With no desk answering nothing is on air to take off, and the air still goes to automation. With no playout layer (`automation_in_ms` null) there is nothing to hand it to. Any staff member's, like the desk's own switches.

put.description: Its cards are drawn first, and a name that cannot fit, or holds characters the card fonts cannot draw, refuses the save (422, with the field named). The presenter's fields (`presenter`, `contact`, `links`, `commercial_music`, `presenter_account`; ADR-0214, ADR-0219) are kept as stored when the body leaves them out, so a client that does not know them never wipes a DJ's details; send an empty value to clear one. A member of staff who is not an admin may name only their own account as `presenter_account` (403 otherwise); an API token may not set it at all. Changing `presenter` or `contact` takes an admin or the show's own presenter (ADR-0241; 403 otherwise); sending them unchanged is fine. `step` (`solo`, `guests`, `callers` or `full`, ADR-0271) is kept as stored when the body leaves it out, and a new show without it starts at `solo`; changing a stored show's step takes an admin, a producer or the show's presenter (403 otherwise; an API token may not), is logged, and takes effect at once if the show is on air.

api_token.description:
An API token (`rsa_…`, ADR-0195) from `POST /api/v1/tokens`, made by an admin for one integration with the scopes it needs. A token reaches only the routes its scopes open (each such route lists `api_token` with the scope it needs) and is never an admin: no route marked `x-admin` takes one. Each token is limited per minute (`429`). The scopes:

- `studio:read`: Read the studio's view: sources, callers (with the names and topics they gave), chat modes, notices; and follow it live.
- `desk:control`: Work the desk: on air, mute, cue, talk, and dump the profanity delay.
- `screener:control`: Work the screener: screen, send, decline and drop callers; end a pass.
- `chat:moderate`: Change the chat's modes (slow mode, hold new, links). The chat's own moderation routes are not reachable with a token.
- `carts:read`: Read the cart wall's banks and carts.
- `carts:fire`: Fire, stop and cue carts; stop the last; fade all.
- `carts:write`: Make and rename banks; load and empty cart slots.
- `schedule:read`: Read the clocks, the week, the log of what is to play, and the episodes airing in a range.
- `schedule:write`: Change clocks, the week and the log; generate a day.
- `playout:read`: Read playout's status and zone, the logger, and the track library.
- `library:write`: Add tracks to the library and delete them.
- `reports:read`: Read the play and audience reports.
- `shows:read`: Read shows, series, episodes and corrections.
- `shows:write`: Change shows, series and episodes; put an episode on air; correct one; publish its files; draw cards.
- `video:read`: Read the video slate's still and the cameras' thumbnails.
- `video:write`: Change or remove the video slate's still.
